Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Holdings' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are David Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Harlan.

David Harlan: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by progress on our strategic initiatives and long-term goals, our management perspective on key industry trends and challenges, robust rate base growth and the factors influencing it, and our investments in renewable energy and the clean energy transition.

Let me provide some more detail on these four key aspects, starting with our progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals. As we close out our third quarter results, we have advanced significantly against our core strategic pillars, setting Nexus Energy Holdings up for enduring success amid the shifting utilities and power generation sector. These pillars center on speeding up the clean energy shift, bolstering grid reliability and toughness, and generating regulated returns via careful capital deployment. This quarter's achievements were bolstered by positive market conditions such as Inflation Reduction Act tax incentives, booming data center electricity needs, and smoother renewable supply chains.

Focusing first on the clean energy shift, central to our net-zero goal by 2045—earlier than peers like Duke Energy or Southern Company—renewables now make up 42% of our generation capacity, risen from 28% two years back. We reached a milestone with 850 MW of fresh solar and wind coming online in Q3, featuring the 450 MW Desert Bloom Solar project in ERCOT, our biggest utility-scale bifacial PV setup yet, hitting a 28.5% first-year capacity factor via advanced single-axis trackers and our AI-based curtailment prediction tools. We're claiming the complete 30% ITC including the domestic content bonus, adding roughly $0.15 per share to annual EPS.

For wind, Phase 1 of the 400 MW Prairie Winds expansion in MISO South went live, using 150-meter towers and 5.5 MW Siemens Gamesa turbines to exceed 45% capacity factors in prime wind zones. Past interconnection holdups—like those NextEra faced—are resolved; we've locked PPAs for 95% of our 5.2 GW pipeline at an average $35/MWh, a 15% bump over 2022 amid inflation and better risk pricing. Storage elevates this: 1.2 GWh of four-hour LFP batteries paired with solar, including a 300 MW/1,200 MWh CAISO system that plays duck curve arbitrage and snags full DOE loan backing. This lifts our dispatchable clean capacity over 2 GW, cutting gas peaker dependence—we idled 15% year-to-date—and yielding LCOE under $25/MWh for new additions.

By region, we're customizing: In the Southeast, second to Southern as a generator, we've shifted 60% of our 1,800 MW legacy coal to gas-renewable hybrids, hastening retirements per EPA Clean Air Act updates. Our Florida arm secured 10-year deals for 600 MW offshore wind leases in the Gulf, teaming with Ørsted for 50+ m/s speeds. In PJM, hyperscalers like Amazon and Microsoft drive 25% of new load, spurring 500 MW behind-the-meter solar-plus-storage for their sites. Midwest hydrogen blending pilots at Ottumwa coal plant mix 5% green H2 from a 100 MW Plug Power electrolyzer JV, priming for 2030 DOE hubs.

On grid reliability, our second pillar, $1.2 billion YTD went to T&D upgrades, 20% ahead of schedule, with 2,500 miles of HTLS reconductored lines slashing outage times 35% in summer peaks. AMI covers 85% of 4.5 million customers, enabling dynamic rates that trimmed Texas peak demand 12% this heatwave. Grid-edge microgrids in California, using Tesla Megapacks tied to SCADA, hit 99.98% uptime amid PG&E wildfires. These yield revenue too—our transmission unit at 10.5% FERC ROE, up 50 bps.

These moves pay off: Regulated capex guided $4.8-5.2 billion yearly, 85% equity-funded with 4.2% debt blend. Consolidated ROE at 9.8%, eyeing 10-11%, renewables adding 2.5 points via PTC/ITC. Customers up 2.8% YoY from EVs—we okayed 150,000 Level 2 chargers—and industrial electrification, adding 1.5 GW firm load by 2026.

M&A-wise, $2.1 billion Midwest Wind Partners buy adds 1.1 GW operating assets at 7.8x EV/EBITDA—bargain vs. Dominion—and accretes $0.20/share. Ties with GE Vernova for 77 MW NuScale SMR in Illinois target 2027 NRC nod, 12% IRR post-45Q.

For long-term, net-zero 2045 reaffirmed, Scope 1&2 emissions down 55% from 2019 TWh-adjusted. Clean capacity to 25 GW by 2030 from 12 GW, 75% mix share, 60-65% payout on 6-8% EPS CAGR. Supply risks like polysilicon or SPP queues hedged—90% turbines secured, suppliers beyond China.

These initiatives propel us, converting regs, innovation, and loads to top returns. We're leading the transition.

Next, our take on industry trends and challenges. We're in a pivotal era with rapid electrification, renewables dominance, and hurdles from regs and supply. U.S. demand to climb 4.7% yearly to 2028 per our IRP, from prior stagnation. AI data centers fuel this—45 GW new load by 2030, 15% of current capacity. Microsoft, Google ink 10-15 year PPAs over $50/MWh in PJM, ERCOT; we nabbed three 200 MW Texas deals 12% above average.

Renewables surge: 35 GW solar/wind 2023, 80% new builds, 12-15% CAGR to 2030 via EIA/WoodMac. BESS doubles to 12 GW yearly, solar+storage factors over 30% vs. 25% prior, via inverters/AI dispatch.

ERCOT (40% of our 15 GW) shines: Q2 spots $45/MWh, $9k peaks; our 1.2 GW peakers, 800 MW batteries thrive. PJM softer, negatives up 25% YoY from surplus, countered by 500 MW wind repower to 45% factors by 2026.

Electrification: EVs to 20% new sales by 2027 per BNEF, 10-15 GW charging. Reshoring semis, H2 adds 5-7 GW Southeast baseload.

Challenges: FERC 2023 queues delay 4-5 years for 2,200 GW; our 1.5 GW risks $150M costs. State RPS tough—CA 100% clean 2045, NY 70% 2030—but ROE squeezed to 9-10% in 12 decoupled states.

Supply: Turbines 18-24 mo from Siemens/Vestas, lithium 40% over pre-COVID. Geopolitics keep natgas $3.50/MMBtu.

Weather: 2023 $5B losses; our Texas O&M up 15% post-Uri hardening.

Our response: $2.5B capex next 3 yrs—60% renewables/storage, 25% grid tech, 15% thermal. Highlights: 1 GW Form Energy iron-air BESS for 100-hr firming, LCOE <$40/MWh; Plug Power 50 MW electrolyzer at coal site, IRA $3/kg PTC for <$2/kg H2 by 2027; ABB GridX AI on 70% assets, +200 bps EBITDA; 400 MW MISO solar PPAs at 11% IRR.

Trends herald $1.2T capex by 2035; we guide 8-10% AFFO FY24, 4.2% yield, 16x P/E.

Third, rate base growth and impacting factors. Our rate base—the net regulated assets like generation, T&D, working capital earning authorized ROE—grew 7.2% YoY to $28.4B in Q3, record for our utility-gen hybrid. TTM $27.9B from $25.1B; FY guide 6.5-7.5% to ~$29.2B.

Powered by $4.2B 2024 capex, 85% regulated/CWIP. $1.8B in-service YTD, AFUDC at WACC.

By class:

Renewables/storage (42% capex, $1.8B): 450 MW solar, 150 MW BESS in Q3, e.g., 300 MW Desert Sun AZ hybrid w/100 MW/400 MWh BESS, 45% IRA ITC via wages/apprentices. YTD 3.1 pts growth; 1.2 GW queued ERCOT/MISO for hyperscaler PPAs.

Transmission/grid (28%, $1.2B): $650M 345 kV PJM lines incl. 50-mi Apex-Penn +1,200 MW; AMI 65% of 2.3M customers for DER/dynamic pricing; FERC 1000/$14B RTEP.

Gas/nuclear (20%, $840M): 2.4 GW CCGT H2-retrofits <6,500 Btu/kWh; 1,800 MW Midwest nuclear life-ext $250M, Prairie Island SGK NRC ok.

Distribution (10%, $420M): 15k L2/200 DC EV chargers, 1,200 mi CA undergrounding per CPUC WMP.

Regional: Southeast 9.1% to $11.2B (AI data 15% load); ERCOT 8.4% $7.8B (Vestas delays); NE MISO/PJM 5.2% $9.4B (trans recoveries).

Impacts: Regs positive—95% forward test/CWIP, GA 10.3% ROE, CPUC $2.1B capex; load +4.2% peak to 28.5 GW, 2.5 GW data; inflation (steel+18%, labor+12%), transfos 150 wk—mitigated hedges; rates debt 4.8%, ATM equity/debt keeps 55% D/E, $180M AFUDC; IRA $450M tax equity, ERCOT BESS 15-20% IRR.

Outlook: "Reliable Renewables"—60% capex clean by 2027, 85% carbon-free factor. SMRs 300 MW NuScale MISO 2030, Palisades restarts. 7-8% CAGR to $35B 2025-27, 6-7% EPS from 9.8% ROE.

Finally, our investments in renewables and clean transition. We've invested heavily here, merging baseload gas/nuclear with renewables scale. 2023 $2.8B clean capex (42% total, +25% YoY); 2024 $3.5B (48%), targeting queue-strong projects amid solar LCOE drops (15% YoY <$0.25/W), 45 GW data load.

Solar leads at 28% of 15 GW portfolio (+10 pts since 2021): 1.2 GW Sun Belt—450 MW Desert Bloom ERCOT bifacial First Solar 15-yr $28/MWh PPA; 500 MW SunForge PJM w/200 MW/800 MWh BESS; 250 MW CAISO Imperial exp. w/$450M ITC transfers. Factors 28-32% via AI O&M (0.4% degr).

Offshore wind: $1.2B 600 MW Gale Force VA w/Ørsted, Siemens 14 MW DD, Q4 2026, 45-50% factor, $45-50/MWh LCOE. Onshore 400 MW SPP repower Vestas V150 +35% out, PTC to 2027.

BESS key: 750 MW/3 GWh YTD, 300 MW/1.2 GWh ERCOT Blackout Buster $85M ancillaries first 6 mo, 92% RTE Tesla; Form iron-air LDES pilots for nuke/H2.

Emerging: $250M green H2, 20 MW Palisades electrolyzer w/Plug 1.4 tpd SPA, DOE hub shortlist; $150M NuScale Utah SMR for AI baseload.

Regional: ERCOT 55% renewables, 80% 2025 hedge $35/MWh; PJM/MISO 2 GW pipe post-FERC 2020, BRA wins; CAISO 800 MW solar+storage 98% capture; India JV 500 MW float solar 12%+ IRR.

Accretive 10-12% ROE vs 8% hurdle, 85% contracted 12-yr AWS/Google/MSFT; IRA compresses equity 40%, $1.2B benefits; carbon -22% to 350 g/kWh, green bonds +40 bps.

Queue 10 GW (60% advanced), 2-3 GW/yr to 2028, 15% EBITDA CAGR. Short timelines, $500M deposits, GE/Nextracker/Sungrow mgmt.

This drives resilient flows in electrification. Our integrated model edges peers like NextEra/Dominion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa to discuss the financials.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3 2024, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.05 and revenue of $3.1 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.3 billion, primarily focused on renewable energy projects and grid modernization. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

David Harlan: Thank you, Lisa. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Sullivan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Sullivan: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for further expansion in renewables and the clean energy transition?

David Harlan: Certainly, Mike. We're aggressively scaling renewables, with solar as the frontrunner at 28% of our portfolio. Recent additions like the 1.2 GW in the Sun Belt, including Desert Bloom and SunForge with integrated BESS, demonstrate our focus on high-efficiency, contracted projects with hyperscalers. Offshore wind like Gale Force and BESS deployments, plus emerging H2 and SMRs, position us for 2-3 GW annual adds from our 10 GW queue, targeting superior returns amplified by IRA credits.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: What is your outlook for rate base growth in 2025 and beyond?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Laura. We're projecting a 7-8% CAGR through 2027, reaching around $35 billion, driven by our $4.2 billion annual capex program with heavy emphasis on renewables, transmission, and grid tech. Tailwinds like load growth from data centers and constructive regs in most jurisdictions support this, with EPS accretion of 6-7% at our 9.8% average ROE, despite some inflation headwinds we've largely hedged.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain bottlenecks and regulatory uncertainties?

Robert Kline: Good question, David. On supply chains, we've hedged 90% of turbine deliveries, diversified beyond China, secured long-term offtakes with Siemens and Vestas, and prioritized short-lead projects. Regulatorily, 95% CWIP/forward test years minimize lag, we're advancing despite FERC queues with deposits, and state incentives like IRA bolster returns. Our tech like AI dispatch and resilient grid upgrades, plus regional diversification, keep us ahead of weather and market volatility.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to David Harlan for closing remarks.

David Harlan: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Energy Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Energy Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
